title: Expression tree canonicalization — Mathematical Expression Search
description: Expressions parse into trees; canonicalization rewrites them into a normal form where equivalent expressions share one representation. Commutative operators sort their operands, variables rename to VAR, constants to NUM. Canonical forms turn structural matching into string equality.

title: Operator tree versus layout tree — Mathematical Expression Search
description: Layout trees capture how an expression looks (fractions, superscripts); operator trees capture what it means. Search by meaning uses operator trees; search by appearance uses layout trees. Choosing the wrong tree is why some formula searches miss obvious equivalents.

title: MathML encoding — Mathematical Expression Search
description: Content MathML encodes operator trees in XML; Presentation MathML encodes layout. Archives store one or both, and search normalizes from either. Standard encodings let tools share formula corpora.

title: LaTeX formula parsing — Mathematical Expression Search
description: Most published math arrives as LaTeX; parsers convert it to operator trees despite LaTeX's layout orientation. title: Subexpression search — Mathematical Expression Search

title: Unification-based matching — Mathematical Expression Search
description: Unification matches patterns with variables against concrete expressions, binding variables consistently. The query 'a + ?x' unifies with 'b + c^2' binding ?x to 'c^2'. Unification gives formula search the power of logic programming.

title: Similarity over exact match — Mathematical Expression Search
description: Exact structural match is brittle; similarity scores count shared subtrees or aligned nodes. Tree edit distance generalizes string edit distance to expression trees. Similarity ranking finds 'close' formulas when nothing matches exactly.
